case_name: Sabbita Satyavathi v Bandala Srinivasarao & Ors.
facts: The wife of the deceased has preferred an appeal by special leave against the judgment and order of the High Court acquitting respondents 1 and 2 of the charge u/s. 302 IPC and convicting them instead u/ss. 326 and 324 IPC respectively.
The occurrence giving rise to the instant appeal is alleged to have taken place at about 6.30 p.m. on January 9, 1992.

The case of the prosecution was that six persons including A-1 and A-2 way laid the deceased and assaulted him with knife, iron rods and sticks as a result of which, he succumbed to his injuries in the hospital.
All the six accused A-1 to A-6 were tried by the Additional Sessions Judge, West Godavari Division, Eluru charged of offences u/ss. 148 and 302 read with S. 149 IPC in Sessions Case No.130 of 1992.
A-1 and A-2 preferred an appeal before the High Court of Judicature Andhra Pradesh at Hyderabad being Criminal Appeal No.238 of 1995.
The High Court by its judgment and order of July 3, 1996 acquitted A-1 and A-2 of the charge u/s. 302 IPC but found them guilty of lesser offences.
issues: Whether the evidence on record justifies the conviction of respondents 1 and 2 under Section 302 IPC.
Whether the High Court was justified in acquitting respondents 1 and 2 of the charge under Section 302 IPC and convicting them instead under Sections 326 and 324 IPC respectively.
petitioner_arguments: The evidence on record clearly establishes an offence u/s. 302 IPC and therefore, the High Court was not justified in acquitting respondents 1 and 2 of the charge u/s. 302 IPC and convicting them u/ss. 326 and 324 IPC respectively.
The prosecution evidence rests on the testimony of three alleged eye witnesses, namely, PWs 2, 3 and 4.
respondent_arguments: The evidence on record is highly suspicious and doubtful and does not justify their conviction at all.
The High Court was justified in acquitting respondents 1 and 2 of the charge under Section 302 IPC and convicting them instead under Sections 326 and 324 IPC respectively.
court_reasoning: We consider it necessary to appreciate the evidence on record since the appeal is wide open before us and not confined to the question of nature of offence or sentence.
The prosecution evidence in this case rests on the testimony of three alleged eye witnesses, namely, PWs 2, 3 and 4.
holding: We allow the appeal and set aside the judgment and order of the High Court acquitting respondents 1 and 2 of the charge u/s. 302 IPC and convicting them instead u/ss. 326 and 324 IPC respectively.
The conviction of respondents 1 and 2 under Sections 326 and 324 IPC respectively is hereby upheld.
